questions.questionText:
A wire is approximately 48cm long and has an approximate diameter of 0.3mm.
Which measuring instruments can be used to obtain more precise values of the dimensions of the
wire?
length of the wire diameter of the wire
Which property of a body results from the effect of a gravitational field on its mass?

options.text: the ability of the body to resist a change in motion

questions.questionText:
A force F acts on a body of mass m for a time t. During this time, the velocity of the body
increases from u to v.
Which equation relates F, m, t, u and v?

An object falls towards the Earth’s surface.
What happens to the gravitational potential energy and to the kinetic energy of the object?
gravitational potential
kinetic energy
energy

In some situations, a force does work.
Which set of conditions increases the quantity of work done by the force?
magnitude distance moved
of force by the force
Which statement about evaporation is correct?

options.text: A body in contact with an evaporating liquid loses thermal energy.
A decrease in the surface area of an evaporating liquid increases the rate of evaporation.
A wind over a liquid decreases the rate of evaporation.
It is necessary to provide an external source of thermal energy to a liquid for it to evaporate.

Which piece of equipment is designed to produce a type of electromagnetic wave?

Wavefronts are incident on a boundary.
What is needed for the wave to refract at the boundary?

options.text: a shiny surface at the boundary
a small gap in the boundary
different mediums either side of the boundary in which the frequency of the wave is different
different mediums either side of the boundary in which the speed of the wave is different

the top of an object O. An inverted image I is formed.
lens
O R S
Which name is given to the distance RS?

The diagram shows the air molecules in part of a sound wave at a particular moment in time.
Which statement is not correct?

options.text: Earlier, there was compression at X.
Later, there will be a rarefaction at X.
This part of the wave is travelling horizontally across the page.
This part of the wave is travelling towards the top of the page.

questions.questionText:
The speed of light in a vacuum is 3.0  108m/s.
Which value is closest to the speed of light in air?

A student is investigating a resistance wire.
She measures the current in a 50cm length of resistance wire.
resistance wire
The student repeats the experiment using a 100cm length of the same resistance wire.
What is the effect of this change on the current in the circuit and on the resistance of the wire?
effect on effect on
current resistance

A resistor is connected to a cell so that there is a current from the positive terminal of the cell to
the negative terminal.
What causes the current in the resistor?

options.text: electrons moving from the negative terminal of the cell to the positive terminal
electrons moving from the positive terminal of the cell to the negative terminal
protons moving from the negative terminal of the cell to the positive terminal
protons moving from the positive terminal of the cell to the negative terminal

questions.questionText:
A plastic rod is rubbed with a dry woollen cloth. The rod becomes positively charged.
Which statement is correct?

options.text: Electrons move from the cloth to the rod.
Electrons move from the rod to the cloth.
Protons move from the cloth to the rod.
Protons move from the rod to the cloth.

charge of 240C passing through the resistor?

The current reading on ammeter 2 is 0.20A.
What is the name for this type of circuit and what is the reading on ammeter 1?
type of circuit reading on ammeter 1

Which metal is used for the core of a transformer?

A thin metal foil is placed in a vacuum. -particles are fired at the foil and most go straight
through. A very small proportion of the -particles are deflected through large angles.
What does this provide evidence for?

options.text: There are negative electrons in each atom.
There is a tiny nucleus in each atom.
There are neutrons in each atom.
